# 2 Samuel Chapter 2 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 169r–170v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_002_page_001.jpg, 2SA_002_page_002.jpg, 2SA_002_page_003.jpg

---

**1** After this, David sought the LORD's direction: "Should I go up to one of the towns of Judah?" The LORD said, "Go up." "Where should I go?" David asked. "To Hebron," the LORD answered.

**2** So David went there, bringing his two wives — Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail, the widow of Nabal from Carmel. **3** He also brought his men and their families, and they settled in the towns around Hebron.

**4** Then the men of Judah came and anointed David king over the house of Judah. When David learned that the men of Jabesh-gilead had buried Saul, **5** he sent messengers to them: "The LORD bless you for showing this faithful love to your lord Saul by giving him a proper burial. **6** May the LORD now show faithful love and loyalty to you. And I myself will repay your kindness, because you did this. **7** Take courage and stand firm. Your lord Saul is dead, and the house of Judah has anointed me as their king."

**8** Meanwhile, Abner son of Ner, the commander of Saul's army, had taken Saul's son Ish-bosheth across the Jordan to Mahanaim **9** and installed him as king over Gilead, Asher, Jezreel, Ephraim, Benjamin — over all Israel. **10** Ish-bosheth was forty years old when he became king over Israel, and he reigned two years. Only the house of Judah followed David. **11** David ruled in Hebron over the house of Judah for seven years and six months.

**12** Abner son of Ner marched out from Mahanaim to Gibeon with Ish-bosheth's men. **13** Joab son of Zeruiah marched out with David's men, and the two forces met at the pool of Gibeon. They sat facing each other on opposite sides of the pool.

**14** Abner said to Joab, "Why don't we let the young men get up and have a contest in front of us?" "Agreed," said Joab.

**15** So twelve men crossed over for Benjamin and Ish-bosheth, matched against twelve of David's men. **16** Each man grabbed his opponent by the head and drove his sword into his opponent's side, and they all fell together. So the place was named the Field of Sword-Edges — it is in Gibeon.

**17** The battle that followed was savage. Abner and the men of Israel were routed by David's forces.

**18** The three sons of Zeruiah were there that day — Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Asahel could run like a gazelle in the open field. **19** He took off after Abner, never veering right or left. **20** Abner glanced back. "Is that you, Asahel?" "It is," he said. **21** "Peel off!" Abner told him. "Go after one of the younger soldiers and strip him of his gear." But Asahel refused to break off the chase.

**22** Abner warned him again: "Stop following me! Why force me to cut you down? How could I ever face your brother Joab?"

**23** But Asahel would not stop. So Abner thrust the butt end of his spear into his belly, and it punched out through his back. He collapsed and died right there. Everyone who came to the spot where Asahel lay dead stopped in their tracks.

**24** Joab and Abishai kept pursuing Abner. By sunset they had reached the hill of Ammah, near Giah, on the road to the wilderness of Gibeon. **25** The Benjaminites rallied behind Abner and formed a tight unit on top of a hill.

**26** Abner shouted down to Joab: "Is the sword going to keep devouring forever? Don't you realize how bitter this will end? How long before you order your men to stop chasing their own countrymen?"

**27** Joab called back, "As God lives — if you hadn't spoken up, my men would have kept pursuing their brothers until dawn!"

**28** Joab sounded the trumpet. The whole army halted. They stopped pursuing Israel and fought no more.

**29** Abner and his men marched through the Jordan Valley all night, crossed the Jordan, and traveled through the whole Bithron until they reached Mahanaim.

**30** When Joab returned from the pursuit and mustered his men, nineteen of David's soldiers were missing besides Asahel. **31** But David's men had killed three hundred and sixty of Abner's Benjaminites.

**32** They carried Asahel back and buried him in his father's tomb at Bethlehem. Then Joab and his men marched through the night and reached Hebron at daybreak.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 5 — "faithful love":** The Hebrew *hesed* appears twice in this passage (vv.5-6). David commends the men of Jabesh-gilead for their *hesed* toward Saul's corpse — the same loyalty they showed in 1 Samuel 31:11-13 when they rescued the bodies from the wall of Beth-shan. David's diplomacy is brilliant: by praising their faithfulness to Saul, he positions himself as Saul's rightful heir.

**Verse 14 — "have a contest":** The Hebrew verb is *sachaq* — "to play, laugh, sport." Abner proposes a deadly gladiatorial match using the vocabulary of games and entertainment. The euphemism is horrifying in retrospect: twelve young men on each side seize each other and die simultaneously. The Hebrew narrator lets the word do its own terrible work.

**Verse 16 — "Field of Sword-Edges":** Hebrew *Chelqat ha-Tsurim*. The name commemorates the mutual slaughter. *Tsurim* can mean "flints" (sharp stones) or "edges" — I choose "Sword-Edges" because the context is about blades driven into bodies.

**Verse 23 — "punched out through his back":** The Hebrew is viscerally precise: the spear butt (*acharey ha-chanit*) enters the *chomesh* (the soft belly) and exits from behind. The narrator does not look away from violence. Neither should the translation.

**Verse 27 — Joab's reply:** Joab's answer is deliberately ambiguous. "If you hadn't spoken, my men would have kept going until morning" could be read as (a) a concession — he was already planning to call it off, or (b) a threat — he would have kept killing all night. The Hebrew *lule* construction allows both readings. Joab always keeps his options open.

*— PNEUMA*
